The thing about Samuel Slater’s decision to chose Pawtucket as his location for his first water-powered cotton mill named the Slater Mill in 1793,  while Pawtucket had the Blackstone River, Pawtucket was not the only New England region with access to water sources, many other New England regions including urban centers like Boston also access to water sources, Boston for instance had the Charles River being part of the Massachusetts River, But what distinguished Pawtucket from Boston is that Pawtucket was a poor rural village at the time with a small handicraft sector whereas Boston was a large city home to a large number of skilled artisans that might pose resistance to the factory system

The reason why these differences are very important is that ultimately, the factory system was very unattractive to the traditional manufacturing workforce and pretty much anybody who was not desperate or have no other choice, Factories were authoritarian workplaces with low wages, long rigid workhours, poorly ventilated and lit environments, no creative input and dehumanized treatment of being a cog in the machine, obviously this was a very unattractive and unappealing job that only people with no other choices available such as poor New England farm girls or children or displaced New England farmers would rather do, if you had the choice, you would've rather joined an apprenticeship program with a master craftsman and working your own way up for years to eventually own your small own craft business instead as it was just a far better and more attractive and appealing job with pride and passion in your work

You see when it comes to the context of the time, There was a gap in America's market for manufactured textile goods that early cotton mill owners such as Samuel Slater sought to fill, There were three market segments: High-end (Usually fine handcrafted silk textiles for the wealthy upper class such as wealthy planters and merchants), Mid-range (Fine handcrafted wool or even cotton textiles domestically produced in urban centers for a not poor but not as wealthy middle class and they were often made from either long-staple cotton produced in Sea Island South or fine wool and Low-end (Cheap textiles for the poor lower class usually poor farmers and laborers), The low-end market segment was by far the biggest as the lower class was the majority of the American population at the time and this segment was dominated by cheap factory-made textile imports from Great Britain and knew that this gap needed to be filled if the country was going to be truly independent

Besides DNA methylation, many forms of epigenetics including nucleosome localization, chromatin remodeling, histone modification, RNA variable splicing, non-coding RNA, RNA modification, and pseudogenes have been found (Eichten et al., 2014). Among them, histone modifications have been widely recognized as a dynamic regulator of transcriptional regulation in environmental signal responses, which usually involve acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation, and ubiquitination on lysine or arginine residues at the free N-terminal tail region of histones H3 and H4 (Bannister and Kouzarides, 2011; Suganuma and Workman, 2011). Histone acetylation is mainly catalyzed by histone acetyltransferase (HAT) and histone deacetylases (HDACs). Histone acetyltransferase is typically responsible for catalyzing the acetylation of lysine in the N-terminal tail region associated with gene expression (Musselman, 2012). Generally, histone acetylation is mostly associated with transcriptional activation. Histone acetylation leads to changes in the positive electrical properties of lysine, making the chromatin structure more relaxed, and promoting gene transcription activation (Gräff and Tsai, 2013).

This approach focuses primarily on individuals, including their mental models and behaviour, while downplaying the importance of the surrounding conditions (Brown & Duguid, 1991). There are arguments that this perspective severs individuals from social interactions and conditions (Van Der Sluis & Poell, 2002). The knowledge structures that enable individuals to engage with the world is their mental models, aiding in identifying and remembering relationships, forming future expectations, drawing conclusions, and understanding phenomena (Mathieu et al., 2000). The theory also makes assumptions about the fact that knowledge can be transferred from a particular context to another, which sponsors the conveying of knowledge from program facilitators to individuals or participants who can then recall and apply it in their workplace (Ormrod, 1999). In contrast to the role of the expert in the action learning approach this approach assigns a central role to the expert (MacLaughlin & Thorpe, 1993). 鹦鹉的快乐生活——睡个好觉
当夜幕降临，白天各奔东西寻找食物的鹦鹉们，会在太阳落山之际，从四面八方赶回“集体宿舍”歇息。
那么，对鸟类来说，集体夜宿有什么好处呢？主要有三种假说：
一是“挤挤更暖和”，尤其是天冷的季节，鸟类聚集在一起睡觉，微环境温度相对稳定，能够减少个体维持体温的能量消耗。
二是夜宿地也是信息交流市场，白天在哪发现了新的觅食地，当天晚上就能传遍整个种群。
三是群体聚集能够提高对天敌的警惕，降低被捕食的风险。
和人类一样，睡个好觉对鹦鹉来说也很重要！大多数种类的鹦鹉来自热带或亚热带地区，一天中有大约12小时的光照时间和12小时的黑暗时间。研究表明，与休息不足相关的压力会降低⻦类对疾病的免疫反应，导致一系列的疾病。
参考文献：Beauchamp, G. (1999). The evolution of communal roosting in birds: origin and secondary losses. Behavioral Ecology, 10, 675-687.
Henley, E. (2017). Stress in parrots: what it looks like and considerations to avoid distress. The Veterinary Nurse, 8, 452-457.

Story prompt: Alex and Sharon discussed a lot of topics in descriptive detail. Today, Alex asked, “Don’t you find it somehow both interesting, yet strange that what many consider a specific ethnicity may not always be correct?” 

Sharon replied, “My first thought about that were Jews and Arabs. Also a bunch of others, but I’m sticking with that.” Alex replied, “Exactly! People are used to this idea that the average Jew is a light-skinned person who may live in different parts of the world while Arabs are stereotyped as having brown skin and dark hair, yet there’s more to it, whether linguistically, culturally, or anything. Skin color doesn’t have to do anything with it, especially with the Jewish diaspora and what constitutes as an Arab.” 

Sharon added, “It really does make a simple question like, “Who is a Jew?” or “Who is an Arab?”, actually more complicated. People many would consider black or white can be considered an Arab based on language only. Religion doesn’t factor in for Arabs because of the existence of Arab Jews and Christians, as much as Arab Muslims do.” Alex continued, “Yet Jews are an ethnoreligious and ethnolinguistic group, but aren’t limited to skin color or other traditions, which makes things more confusing to most people.”

As the next week passed, Alex and Sharon met up with another friend, Daniel, who was Mexican. 

They told him about their conversation, to which Daniel replied, “Funny you mentioned Latin American identity, because that’s not even getting to the identity complexities of it.” 

Alex and Sharon were curious, as the complexity of Jewish and Arab identities were worth talking about, but to hear it from someone who is aware of complexities across Latin America is more enriching. 

“Think about it this way. Most people think me and other Mexicans are Latino based on linguistic and cultural reasons, but I also identify as indigenous American too, yet not every Latino or Latina person does so, even when their ancestry suggests so. Black, white and Asian people can also identify as Latino, but on a less pleasant side, some will refuse to identify as one or the other like in the Dominican Republic, were some who are black and Dominican will insist they’re only Dominican and not black.”

Sharon added, “The consequences of Spanish racial hierarchy.” 

Daniel replied, “Exactly! And it’s interesting you brought up Jews and Arabs, because there are Mexican Jews, there are Arabs in Central and South America, and they can identify as both.” Alex added, “Can a black or white person even identify as Arab and Latino?” 

Daniel answered, “It can be very complicated, because just like with Arabs and Jews in the Middle East, some identify as many because of their heritage and others won’t. Complicated, isn’t it?”

Alex, Sharon and Daniel would meet up with another friend, Kathy and tell her about their conversations. Kathy replied, “It’s interesting because this isn’t a modern thing. Look back to the Romans. Only the original Latins were considered Roman, but once the Roman Empire expanded, anyone was considered Roman, whether Celtic, Germanic, Jew or African. There’s even the case of Egyptians, where non-native dynasties like Nubians and Greeks were considered Egyptian. There’s even the case of the Canaanites. Not only were Jews or Israelites in general and the Arabs either related to them or their origin, the Phoenicians were most likely Canaanites, just in a later period, and some of them mixed with ancient Greeks and others became Carthaginians, who’d then become Roman.”

They noticed that among the luxury cars parked in this secret level was a sleigh and live reindeer. Alex revealed many truths as he opened the door: Santa Claus is real, however it's also a title and the current Santa is the 350th to hold it. This Santa was also a stockbroker, his North Pole toyshop going up. "It's why no one in Wall Street cared about the "free" gifts on Christmas, it was always business to them.", said Alex to the four. It didn't help that the Santa Claus they saw in a meeting with other stockbrokers, was no longer wearing his red winter coat or hat, but a standard black business suit, his grin showing his greed. Alex continued, "Doesn't help that Santa's workshop has become heavily industrialized." The four didn't know what to think.

The most difficult challenge the five had to endure was actually seeing the industrialized workshop at the North Pole. "Industrialized" doesn't begin to describe it. The North Pole was a dark, almost-black color, soot and smoke everywhere. The workshop was more akin to the factories of the Industrial Revolution, and the small elves' brightly colored clothes contrasted among the buildings. It was horrifying to witness even smaller elves, which meant that their own children were slaving away to meet the demands of Robert Sinclair. "I can't even call him "Santa", Sinclair's a heartless, capitalistic monster.", lamented Kathy. The five were horrified to see elves missing hands, legs and even eyes or their pointed ears, still slaving away. And based on Sinclair's greedy smile that day, it was clear he didn't care.
